column2: 3.1 Currency and completeness

Is there a pre-defined approach to ensure that metadata is kept up-to-date?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe your approach.
column4:
Newly opened datasets are required to update the data with the periodicity specified in the metadata. Data user can see if the periodisity value of data set consides date of the last update. In future foreseen implement an automatic mechanism for such verification.

Currently we are in process implementing DCAT extensions to add metadata for each data field, we have to special data field types temporal and spatial. If data provider specified temporal or spatial types, then we are able to automatically detect and update temporal and spatial coverage.
column7:
Datasets that have recently been made available must be regularly updated according to the frequency outlined in the metadata. Users are now getting automatic notifications if the dataset is not being updated. They can also check manually if the dataset's periodicity aligns with the date of its last update. 
At present, we're in the final stage of implementing DCAT extensions to incorporate metadata for every data field. This includes specialized types for temporal and spatial data fields. By specifying temporal or spatial types, data providers enable us to automatically identify and update temporal and spatial coverage.

column2:
What percentage of the metadata on the national portal is obtained from the source automatically, rather than edited manually? 

For Explanation:
* Please describe (1) the workflows you have to automate the harvesting of metadata and (2) for which types of data these apply to
column7: When data is updated in data storage, the metadata on the portal is also automatically updated through synchronization. This includes fields like "Updated" (date when metadata was updated), "Data Structure", "Data", etc. Additionally, metadata updates are automatically pulled from external catalogs such as atvirfinansai.lt and geoportal.lt, although these updates are currently paused pending the alignment of the Inspire and DCAT standards.

column2:
What is the average delay from the moment the metadata describing a dataset is updated at the source, and the moment the change is visible on the portal?

For Explanation:
* Please explain the approach for updating metadata in a timely manner
column7: Metadata is updated on a periodic basis, which differs for each dataset (yearly, monthly, weekly, daily, etc.). Typically, organizations configure their systems to update metadata automatically via API. When the scheduled time for an update arrives, according to the established periodicity, the metadata is updated within one day. Additionally, when data is updated in the data storage, this change is reflected almost immediately on the portal

column2:

For Explanation:

column7:
We adhere to the open data principles that are outlined and published on the portal. https://old.data.gov.lt/opening/learningmaterial/16
When a data source is specified for a dataset, it includes information such as the publication date of the dataset, the period it covers, and its update history. After a complete inventory of possible open sources, there will be an opportunity for a qualitative assessment of the application of the implementation of the principles.

column2:
Do you set any standards on metadata quality that data providers must abide by (e.g. on the use of licence, minimum metadata describes, use of certain DCAT-AP properties, etc)

For Explanation:
* If yes, please describe the standards you have in place, i.e. what is minimum information the metadata should describe
column7:
In order to maintain high-quality metadata, we employ a data maturity level rating system developed by Tim Berners-Lee, known as the 5-star deployment scheme for open data. This system primarily evaluates the format and accessibility of the data, ensuring that it meets established standards. More information about this rating system at https://5stardata.info/en/.
Dataset data structure has an option to add a property from other vocabularies/ontologies, including DCAT-AP. To access it, user needs to edit a dataset and put the property into "Class" field.

3.4 Deployment quality and linked data

Do you use a model (such as the 5-Star Open Data or FAIR) to assess the quality of deployment of data in your country?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe.
column4: We use 5-5tar Open Data model. At the dataset level we assign stars based on distribution format used. But at individual data field level, stars from 0 to 3 are assigned manually, but 4 and 5 are detected automatically by checking if a data model has a primary key if field is a reference to another data model and if an association with external vocabulary is provided. So first at dataset level we have a very approximate rating, but on data fields level, we have a very precise rating.
column7: We utilize the 5-star Tim-Berners Lee model to assess data quality. While the overall dataset is evaluated based on its format, the rating of individual fields varies. This variation is determined by factors such as the data's relationships with other datasets, whether it includes a primary key, etc.

column2:

For Explanation:

column4: Yes, we ask data providers to provide data structure description tables. With help of such tables and companion automated tools, we are able to increase data queality quite easily. If data itself is in good shape, then the rest is mostly matter of filling in some additional metadata about individual data fields. We keep track of data quality for each individual data fields and data users can easily request to miproved data maturity of each data field or even collaborate and provide missing metadat themselves, which can imporove data quality.
column7: We have implemented ADP functionality that enables users to submit requests for correcting errors in datasets, thereby enhancing the quality of the data.
